summary: Verified iteration-52 heavy-queue + cache + streaming refactor + frontend button-lock. All 6 backend integration tests pass (sales-report shape+cache, monthly-profit streaming, sales-reconciliation streaming, 10-req concurrent burst all 200 + /api/stats alive, sales-manager-report regression). Frontend: admin login OK, /sales-report ALL button loads data (1 stamp row / 264 items), month buttons + year-select verified DISABLED during load (as designed), Purchase List loads 296 rows, Profit Analysis page loads. Button-lock works: when clicking month-1/2/3 rapidly, disabled buttons natively suppress subsequent clicks in browser, so users cannot cause stale-data flashes.
critical_code_review_comments: SalesReport.jsx: Because month buttons are disabled during load, native browsers already suppress subsequent clicks — the reqSeq guard is defensive/redundant but harmless. Consider adding a subtle 'Loading...' indicator so users understand why buttons appear unresponsive after a click.

server.py: heavy_queue infra (_heavy_gate semaphore=2, _report_cache TTL 5min) is sound; ensure _inv_cache.invalidate() also clears _report_cache (task states this is done — verified by cache-hit test).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login response uses key 'access_token' (not 'token'). Preview DB is small (~500 txns 2025) — heavy endpoints respond <1s so real 503/queue-timeout paths cannot be triggered here; only correctness + concurrency-no-crash was verified. Sales-report shape: by_stamp/by_item/totals; by_item rows include stock_sale_ratio, avg_stock_kg, merged_names. Monthly-profit uses key 'all_items' + 'total_net_wt_sold'. Sales-reconciliation uses 'grand_totals_all_items' as totals-like key.
